We also recommend that a\n      file or class name and description of purpose be included on the\n      same \"printed page\" as the copyright notice for easier\n      identification within third-party archives.\n\n   Copyright [yyyy] [name of copyright owner]\n\n   Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the \"License\");\n   you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.\n   You may obtain a copy of the License at\n\n       http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0\n\n   Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software\n   distributed under the License is distributed on an \"AS IS\" BASIS,\n   WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.\n   See the License for the specific language governing permissions and\n   limitations under the License.\n\n\nhttps://raw.githubusercontent.com/pinder-org/pinder/ebeb28a2f8411363cef722b7d293c978f7442672/README.md\n![pinder](https://github.com/pinder-org/pinder/raw/main/assets/pinder.png)\n<div align=\"center\">\n    <h1>PINDER: The Protein INteraction Dataset and Evaluation Resource</h1>\n</div>\n\n---\n\n[![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/pinder)](https://pypi.org/project/pinder/)\n[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](https://github.com/pinder-org/pinder/blob/master/LICENSE)\n[![GitHub Repo stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/pinder-org/pinder)](https://github.com/pinder-org/pinder/stargazers)\n[![test](https://github.com/pinder-org/pinder/actions/workflows/pr.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/pinder-org/pinder/actions/workflows/pr.yaml)\n[![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/pinder-org/pinder/graph/badge.svg?token=NPQAYW75OD)](https://codecov.io/gh/pinder-org/pinder)\n\n# 📚 About\n\n**pinder**, short for **p**rotein **in**teraction **d**ataset and **e**valuation **r**esource, is a dataset and resource for training and evaluation of protein-protein docking algorithms. It is ~500x larger than previous state of the art datasets and is the first dataset to include paired predicted and apo structures to train flexible docking methods.\n\nThe complete dataset contains approximately 1.04 TB of files and is hosted on Cloudflare R2 at https://pinderdata.org.\n\n# 👨‍💻 Getting Started\n\n## Prerequisites\n\n### fastpdb support\n\npinder uses [fastpdb](https://github.com/biotite-dev/fastpdb) to accelerate PDB\nI/O operations. fastpdb is a dependency of pinder-core, and pip will attempt to\ninstall it for you during the installation of pinder. Pre-built wheels of\nfastpdb are available on PyPI for the following platforms:\n1. Linux with `glibc>=2.34` (e.g., Debian 12, Ubuntu 22.04, RHEL 9, etc.)\n2. MacOS Sierra (10.12) or newer\n3. Windows\n\nIf your platform doesn't match these conditions, you will not get a wheel and\npip will attempt to build fastpdb from source. In order to build fastpdb from\nsource, you will need the rust toolchain, which you can install by running:\n\n```bash\ncurl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh\n```\n\nbefore installing pinder.\n\n## Install pinder\n\n### Initialize a virtual environment or conda environment\n\nWe recommend installing pinder into a clean virtual environment or conda\nenvironment. This can be done using\n[`mamba`](https://github.com/mamba-org/mamba) or `conda` (you can swap `mamba`\nfor `conda` for the same functionality):\n\n\n```bash\nmamba create --name pinder python=3.11\nmamba activate pinder\n```\n\n\nor via `venv` from the Python standard library:\n\n```bash\n# clone the repo and cd into it, unless you plan to install from PyPI, then\npython3 -m venv venv\nsource venv/bin/activate\n```\n\n## Install optional dependencies\n\n### pytorch-cluster\n\n`pytorch-cluster` is an optional dependency for pinder. If you wish to make use\nof its features, you will need to install it separately.\n\nTo install from a wheel, run\n\n```bash\npip install torch-cluster -f https://data.pyg.org/whl/torch-${TORCH}+${CUDA}.html\n```\n\nwhere `${TORCH}` should be replaced by the version of PyTorch installed and `${CUDA}` should be replaced by either `cpu`, `cu118`, or `cu121`\ndepending on your PyTorch installation.\n\nTo install from source, first make sure you have pytorch installed in the\ncurrent environment (`pip install torch`), then run\n\n```bash\npip install torch-cluster\n```\n\nNote that on Apple Silicon MacOS machines, installation from source is the only option.\n\n### PRODIGY-cryst\n\nPRODIGY-cryst is used in the data ingestion pipeline to predict the probability that an interface is a biological interaction. While it is not needed to use `pinder.core`, it is an optional dependency of `pinder.data` and can be installed as a git-based installation. Default is None (all available cores).\n```\n\nThe expected format for the contents of `eval_dir` are shown below:\n```\neval_dir_example/\n└── some_method\n    ├── 1an1__A1_P00761--1an1__B1_P80424\n    │   ├── apo_decoys\n    │   │   ├── model_1.pdb\n    │   │   └── model_2.pdb\n    │   ├── holo_decoys\n    │   │   ├── model_1.pdb\n    │   │   └── model_2.pdb\n    │   └── predicted_decoys\n    │       ├── model_1.pdb\n    │       └── model_2.pdb\n    └── 1b8m__A1_P23560--1b8m__B1_P34130\n        ├── holo_decoys\n        │   ├── model_1.pdb\n        │   └── model_2.pdb\n        └── predicted_decoys\n            ├── model_1.pdb\n            └── model_2.pdb\n```\n\nThe eval directory should contain one or more methods to evaluate as sub-directories.\n\nEach method sub-directory should contains sub-directories that are named by pinder system ID.\n\nInside of each pinder system sub-directory, you should have three subdirectories:\n* `holo_decoys` (predictions that were made using holo monomers)\n* `apo_decoys` (predictions made using apo monomers)\n* `predicted_decoys` (predictions made using predicted, e.g. AF2, monomers)\n\nYou can have any number of decoys in each directory; however, the decoys should be named in a way that the prediction rank can be extracted. It is ~500x larger than previous state of the art datasets and is the first dataset to include paired predicted and apo structures to train flexible docking methods.\n\nThe complete dataset contains approximately 1.04 TB of files and is hosted on Cloudflare R2 at https://pinderdata.org.\n\n# 👨‍💻 Getting Started\n\n## Prerequisites\n\n### fastpdb support\n\npinder uses [fastpdb](https://github.com/biotite-dev/fastpdb) to accelerate PDB\nI/O operations. fastpdb is a dependency of pinder-core, and pip will attempt to\ninstall it for you during the installation of pinder. Pre-built wheels of\nfastpdb are available on PyPI for the following platforms:\n1. Linux with `glibc>=2.34` (e.g., Debian 12, Ubuntu 22.04, RHEL 9, etc.)\n2. MacOS Sierra (10.12) or newer\n3. Windows\n\nIf your platform doesn't match these conditions, you will not get a wheel and\npip will attempt to build fastpdb from source. In order to build fastpdb from\nsource, you will need the rust toolchain, which you can install by running:\n\n```bash\ncurl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh\n```\n\nbefore installing pinder.\n\n## Install pinder\n\n### Initialize a virtual environment or conda environment\n\nWe recommend installing pinder into a clean virtual environment or conda\nenvironment. This can be done using\n[`mamba`](https://github.com/mamba-org/mamba) or `conda` (you can swap `mamba`\nfor `conda` for the same functionality):\n\n\n```bash\nmamba create --name pinder python=3.11\nmamba activate pinder\n```\n\n\nor via `venv` from the Python standard library:\n\n```bash\n# clone the repo and cd into it, unless you plan to install from PyPI, then\npython3 -m venv venv\nsource venv/bin/activate\n```\n\n## Install optional dependencies\n\n### pytorch-cluster\n\n`pytorch-cluster` is an optional dependency for pinder. If you wish to make use\nof its features, you will need to install it separately.\n\nTo install from a wheel, run\n\n```bash\npip install torch-cluster -f https://data.pyg.org/whl/torch-${TORCH}+${CUDA}.html\n```\n\nwhere `${TORCH}` should be replaced by the version of PyTorch installed and `${CUDA}` should be replaced by either `cpu`, `cu118`, or `cu121`\ndepending on your PyTorch installation.\n\nTo install from source, first make sure you have pytorch installed in the\ncurrent environment (`pip install torch`), then run\n\n```bash\npip install torch-cluster\n```\n\nNote that on Apple Silicon MacOS machines, installation from source is the only option.\n\n### PRODIGY-cryst\n\nPRODIGY-cryst is used in the data ingestion pipeline to predict the probability that an interface is a biological interaction. While it is not needed to use `pinder.core`, it is an optional dependency of `pinder.data` and can be installed as a git-based installation. To install, run\n\n```bash\npip install git+https://github.com/yusuf1759/prodigy-cryst.git\n```\n\n### Install pinder packages from PyPI\n\nTo install with the minimal dependencies needed to use `pinder.core`\n```bash\npip install pinder\n```\n\nInstall optional extras, for instance to use the `pinder.eval` package\n\n```bash\npip install pinder[eval]\n```\n\nOr, install all extras\n\n```bash\npip install pinder[all]\n```\n\n\n# ⬇️ Getting the dataset\n\nWe strongly recommend to interact via the provided python API in `pinder-core`, as follows, which will automatically download and load the data into either `$PINDER_BASE_DIR` or `$XDG_DATA_HOME` (usually `~/.local/share/pinder` on Mac and Linux) if no explicit download path is provided (recommended)\n\nNOTE: the default location for the dataset is `~/.local/share/pinder/<release version>`\n\nIf you want to use a different location, you can do so by setting the `PINDER_BASE_DIR` environment variable.\n\nThe base dir refers to a fully qualified path name up until the `<release version>` (not inclusive).\n\nFor instance, you could:\n```bash\nexport PINDER_BASE_DIR=~/my-custom-location-for-pinder/pinder\n```\n\nYou can always check the current location of the dataset like so:\n```python\nfrom pinder.core import get_pinder_location\nget_pinder_location()\n```\n\nThe current release version of pinder is `2024-02`.\n\nYou can find the list of available dataset releases and the associated changes in the [data changelog](https://github.com/pinder-org/pinder/blob/main/changelog_data.md).\n\n## Download archives and sync the complete dataset\n\n```bash\npinder_download\npinder_sync_data\n```\n\n`pinder_download` downloads and extracts the published archives. The archives\ndo not contain every file in the release manifests. Run `pinder_sync_data`\nafter extraction to download the missing structure and mapping files and verify\ntheir checksums. Existing files are skipped without checksum verification and\nare not replaced. The index and metadata are downloaded automatically when\nfirst accessed through `get_index()` and `get_metadata()`.\n\nTo inspect the archive download options:\n\n```\npinder_download --help\n\nusage: Download latest pinder dataset to disk [-h] [--pinder_base_dir PINDER_BASE_DIR] [--pinder_release PINDER_RELEASE] [--skip_inflation]\n\noptional arguments:\n  -h, --help            show this help message and exit\n  --pinder_base_dir PINDER_BASE_DIR\n                        specify a non-default pinder base directory\n  --pinder_release PINDER_RELEASE\n                        specify a pinder dataset version\n  --skip_inflation      if passed, will only download the compressed archives without unpacking\n```\n\nThe full dataset should look like this:\n\n```bash\nget_pinder_location()/\n    pdbs/\n    test_set_pdbs/\n    mappings/\n    index.parquet\n    metadata.parquet\n```\n\n* `pdbs/` contains individual monomer and ground-truth dimer PDB structures\n* `mappings/` contains mapping information for holo and apo monomers for PDB<->uniprot, as well as original PDB assembly information used in some utilities\n* `index.parquet` contains the master index of every dimer in pinder. See [here](https://pinder-org.github.io/pinder/pinder-index.html) for more details.\n* `metadata.parquet` contains additional metadata detail for each entry in the index.\n\nDownloads are served from `https://pinderdata.org/2024-02/`. Use\n`pinder_download` above to download archives with checksum verification and\nresume during automatic retries.\n\nFor the default archive-download-and-sync workflow, allow at least **1.2 TB of\nfree disk space**, including room for filesystem overhead. Sizes below use\ndecimal units (1 GB = 1,000,000,000 bytes) and describe the `2024-02` release:\n\n| Data | Compressed archive | Complete directory from manifest |\n| --- | ---: | ---: |\n| PDB structures | 168.88 GB | 1,013.35 GB |\n| Test-set structures | 0.18 GB | 0.73 GB |\n| Mappings | 7.23 GB | 23.83 GB |\n\nThe archives total approximately 176.3 GB; the complete directories total\napproximately 1.04 TB. `pinder_download` removes each archive after extraction.\nKeeping archives with `--skip_inflation` and later retaining them alongside the\ncomplete dataset requires additional space.\n\n## Updating the dataset\nIn the event that there are patch (non-breaking) changes to the index or metadata, you can sync your local copy of the index using a similar command-line interface:\n\n```\npinder_update_index --help\n\nusage: Download latest pinder index to disk [-h] [--pinder_base_dir PINDER_BASE_DIR] [--pinder_release PINDER_RELEASE] [--skip_inflation]\n\noptional arguments:\n  -h, --help            show this help message and exit\n  --pinder_base_dir PINDER_BASE_DIR\n                        specify a non-default pinder base directory\n  --pinder_release PINDER_RELEASE\n                        specify a pinder dataset version\n```\n\nTo fetch additional structure or mapping files listed in the release manifests,\nrun `pinder_sync_data`. \n| `-lg [filename]`          | master.log    | log filename\n| `-rt [integer]`           | 0             | the number of retries\n\n\n## Example of docking table (.table)\n\nParameters and docking target list should be written in a text file.\nA table file should have `TITLE` and `PARAM` lines followed by parameters listed by the same order as in the `PARAM` line.\n`SAMPLE.table` file in this package shows an example.\n\n- [data/SAMPLE.table](data/SAMPLE.table)\n\n```\nTITLE=sample jobs\nPARAM=-R $1 -L $2 -O\ndata/1gcq_r.pdb\tdata/1gcq_r.pdb\ndata/1gcq_r.pdb\tdata/1gcq_l.pdb\ndata/1gcq_l.pdb\tdata/1gcq_r.pdb\ndata/1gcq_l.pdb\tdata/1gcq_l.pdb\n```\n\nYou can specify docking parameters loaded by MEGADOCK by setting `PARAM` in the table file.\nLines follows the `PARAM` lines specifies parameters for each docking job which will be distributed to available nodes by MPI.\n\n### More details about parameters for each docking calculation\n\n- [See above section](#Parametersfor-docking-calculation)\n\n----\n\n# Thread parallelization (OpenMP)\n\nMEGADOCK parallelizes rotation calculations by using OpenMP.\nYou can specify the number of OpenMP threads for parallel calculations by environmental variable such as `$OMP_NUM_THREADS`.\n\n```sh\n# e.g.) megadock binary using 8 OpenMP threads\nexport OMP_NUM_THREADS=8\n./megadock -R data/receptor.pdb -L data/ligand.pdb -o data/receptor_ligand.out\n\n# e.g.) each MPI process uses 8 OpenMP threads\nmpirun -n 4 -x OMP_NUM_THREADS=8  ./megadock-dp -tb data/SAMPLE.table\n```\n\n----\n\n\n# Generate decoy from docking output\n\nEach docking job generates docking output file in which rotation angles (x, y, z) of ligand from the initial structure, numbers of voxel translation (x, y, z) from receptor center coordinate and docking scores are listed.  \n\nIf you want to generate decoy pdbfiles, please use `decoygen` command. It is generated together with MEGADOCK binary.\n\n## Command Usage\n\n```sh\n./decoygen [decoy_filename] [used_ligand.pdb] [.outfile] [decoy no.]\n```\n\n\n## Command Example\n\nFor example, the megadock output file was generated as `dock.out` using `rec.pdb` as receputer input and `lig.pdb` as ligand output, and you want to **generate 1st ranked decoy**.\n\n```sh\n# megadock docking calculation\nmegadock -R rec.pdb -L lig.pdb -o dock.out\n\n# generate 1st ranked decoy\n./decoygen lig.1.pdb lig.pdb dock.out 1\ncat rec.pdb lig.1.pdb > decoy.1.pdb\n\n# lig.1.pdb   : rotated and translated lig.pdb\n# decoy.1.pdb : complex pdb file\n```\n\nIf you want to generate all decoys;\n\n```sh\n# megadock docking calculation\nmegadock -R rec.pdb -L lig.pdb -o dock.out\n\n# generate all decoys\nfor i in `seq 1 2000`; do ./decoygen lig.${i}.pdb lig.pdb dock.out $i; cat rec.pdb lig.${i}.pdb > decoy.${i}.pdb; done\n```\n\n----\n\n# Blocking target residues\n\n`block` tool (python script) is to block some residues of a receptor protein from docking.\nIf you know that some residues are not in the binding sides, please list their residue numbers and input `block` tool.\nThis program changes the name of residues to \"BLK\" and prints the new pdb on the screen.\n\n```sh\n./block [pdbfile] [chain] [target residue list]\n# ex)\n# ./block 1gcq_r.pdb B 182-186,189,195-198,204 > blocked.pdb\n```\n\nTarget residues list is separated by commas and no spaces.\nYou can also use `-` (hyphen): \"182-186\" means blocking residues of 182, 183, ..., 186.\nBlocked residues are substituted for 'BLK'.\nUpdated PDB coordinates are written to \"standard output\". Output PPI score\n./ppiscore dock.out 10800\n```\n\n### Note\n\n`ppiscore` is compatible with re-ranking tools to get better docking candidates (e.g. [ZRANK1](http://zdock.umassmed.edu/software/)) and those tools can be used for the output files of docking calculation using megadock.\nIf you want to use such reranking tools, please refer to [our website documentation](http://www.bi.cs.titech.ac.jp/megadock/ppi.html).\n\nFor more details about `ppiscore`, please check [our webpage documentation](http://www.bi.cs.titech.ac.jp/megadock/ppi.html) or following references.\n\n----\n\n\n## References\n\n- Masahito Ohue, Takehiro Shimoda, Shuji Suzuki, Yuri Matsuzaki, Takashi Ishida, Yutaka Akiyama. (Default: `sm_60`)\n\nmegadock_commands.md\n# Command Guide\n\nThis documentation show the command usage and examples for protein-protein docking calculation using MEGADOCK.\nIf you do not have any MEGADOCK binary, please read the build documentation ([doc/BUILD.md](./BUILD.md)).\n\n> Note: The sample input files (`.pdb`, `.table`) are stored in `data` directory.\n\n\n## Section Link\n\nPlease select your target environment and check the command example.\n\n| Type | Target Env.     | Binary             | Note \n|:----:|-----------------|--------------------| :-\n|  (a) | [GPU cluster](#command-for-multiple-nodes-environment) | `megadock-gpu-dp`  | multiple nodes\n|  (b) | [CPU cluster](#command-for-multiple-nodes-environment) | `megadock-dp`      | multiple nodes\n|  (c) | [GPU node](#command-for-single-node-environment)      | `megadock-gpu`     | single node\n|  (d) | [CPU node](#command-for-single-node-environment)      | `megadock`         | single node\n\nOther Commands:\n\n| Command    | Note\n| :-         | :-\n| `decoygen` | [Generate decoy pdb files from docking output](#Generate-decoy-from-docking-output)\n| `block`    | [Blocking target residues](#Blocking-target-residues)\n| `ppiscore` | [Protein-Protein interaction prediction](#Protein-Protein-interaction-prediction)\n\n----\n\n# Command for Single Node Environment\n\nTarget Environments:\n  - (c) Compile for GPU node (GPU)\n  - (d) Compile for CPU node (only thread parallelization)\n\n## Command example\n\n```sh\n# (c) GPU single node\n./megadock-gpu -R receptor.pdb -L ligand.pdb -o receptor-ligand.out\n\n# (d) CPU single node\n./megadock -R receptor.pdb -L ligand.pdb -o receptor-ligand.out\n```\n\n### Run small sample\n\n```sh\n# (c) GPU single node\n./megadock-gpu -R data/1gcq_r.pdb -L data/1gcq_l.pdb -o data/1gcq_r-1gcq_l.out\n\n# (d) CPU single node\n./megadock -R data/1gcq_r.pdb -L data/1gcq_l.pdb -o data/1gcq_r-1gcq_l.out\n```\n\n## Parameters for docking calculation\n\n| Required            | Note\n| :-------------------| :-\n| `-R [filename]`     | receptor pdb file (input)\n| `-L [filename]`     | ligand pdb file (input)\n\n\n| Optional                  | default       | Note\n| :------------------------ | :------------ | :-- \n| `-o [filename]`           | $R-$L.out     | output filename (output)\n| `-O`                      |               | output docking detail files\n| `-N [integer]`            | 2000          | set the number of output predictions\n| `-t [integer]`            | 1             | set the number of predictions per each rotation\n| `-F [integer]`            |               | set the number of FFT point (default: none)\n| `-v [float]`              | 1.2 (angstrom)| set the voxel pitch size\n| `-D`                      |               | set the 6 deg. (54000 angles) of rotational sampling (default to none, 15 deg. (3600 angles) of rotational sampling)\n| `-r [integer]`            | 3600          | set the number of rotational sampling angles (54000: 54000 angles, 1: 1 angles, 24: 24 angles, default to 3600 angles)\n| `-e [float]`              | 1.0           | set the electrostatics term ratio\n| `-d [float]`              | 1.0           | set the hydrophobic term ratio\n| `-a [float]`              | -45.0         | set the rPSC receptor core penalty\n| `-b [float]`              | 1.0           | set the rPSC ligand core penalty\n| `-f [1/2/3]`              | 3             | set function (1: rPSC only, 2: rPSC+Elec, 3: rPSC+Elec+RDE, default to 3)\n| `-h`                      |               | show command help\n\n\n----\n\n# Command for Multiple Nodes Environment\n\nTarget Environments:\n- (a) Compile for GPU cluster (GPU & MPI)\n- (b) Compile for CPU cluster (MPI)\n\n## Command example\n\n```sh\n# (a) GPU & MPI (e.g. 4 MPI processes)\nmpirun -n 4 ./megadock-gpu-dp -tb data/SAMPLE.table\n\n# (b) CPU & MPI (e.g. 4 MPI processes)\nmpirun -n 4 ./megadock-dp -tb data/SAMPLE.table\n```\n\n\n## Parameters for parallel execution\n\n| Required                     | Note\n| :----------------------------| :-\n| `-tb [filename] `            | docking table (.table)\n\n\n| Optional                  | default       | Note\n| :------------------------ | :------------ | :-- \n| `-lg [filename]`          | master.log    | log filename\n| `-rt [integer]`           | 0             | the number of retries\n\n\n## Example of docking table (.table)\n\nParameters and docking target list should be written in a text file.\nA table file should have `TITLE` and `PARAM` lines followed by parameters listed by the same order as in the `PARAM` line.\n`SAMPLE.table` file in this package shows an example.\n\n- [data/SAMPLE.table](data/SAMPLE.table)\n\n```\nTITLE=sample jobs\nPARAM=-R $1 -L $2 -O\ndata/1gcq_r.pdb\tdata/1gcq_r.pdb\ndata/1gcq_r.pdb\tdata/1gcq_l.pdb\ndata/1gcq_l.pdb\tdata/1gcq_r.pdb\ndata/1gcq_l.pdb\tdata/1gcq_l.pdb\n```\n\nYou can specify docking parameters loaded by MEGADOCK by setting `PARAM` in the table file.\nLines follows the `PARAM` lines specifies parameters for each docking job which will be distributed to available nodes by MPI.\n\n### More details about parameters for each docking calculation\n\n- [See above section](#Parametersfor-docking-calculation)\n\n----\n\n# Thread parallelization (OpenMP)\n\nMEGADOCK parallelizes rotation calculations by using OpenMP.\nYou can specify the number of OpenMP threads for parallel calculations by environmental variable such as `$OMP_NUM_THREADS`.\n\n```sh\n# e.g.) megadock binary using 8 OpenMP threads\nexport OMP_NUM_THREADS=8\n./megadock -R data/receptor.pdb -L data/ligand.pdb -o data/receptor_ligand.out\n\n# e.g.) each MPI process uses 8 OpenMP threads\nmpirun -n 4 -x OMP_NUM_THREADS=8  ./megadock-dp -tb data/SAMPLE.table\n```\n\n----\n\n\n# Generate decoy from docking output\n\nEach docking job generates docking output file in which rotation angles (x, y, z) of ligand from the initial structure, numbers of voxel translation (x, y, z) from receptor center coordinate and docking scores are listed.  \n\nIf you want to generate decoy pdbfiles, please use `decoygen` command. It is generated together with MEGADOCK binary.\n\n## Command Usage\n\n```sh\n./decoygen [decoy_filename] [used_ligand.pdb] [.outfile] [decoy no.]\n```\n\n\n## Command Example\n\nFor example, the megadock output file was generated as `dock.out` using `rec.pdb` as receputer input and `lig.pdb` as ligand output, and you want to **generate 1st ranked decoy**.\n\n```sh\n# megadock docking calculation\nmegadock -R rec.pdb -L lig.pdb -o dock.out\n\n# generate 1st ranked decoy\n./decoygen lig.1.pdb lig.pdb dock.out 1\ncat rec.pdb lig.1.pdb > decoy.1.pdb\n\n# lig.1.pdb   : rotated and translated lig.pdb\n# decoy.1.pdb : complex pdb file\n```\n\nIf you want to generate all decoys;\n\n```sh\n# megadock docking calculation\nmegadock -R rec.pdb -L lig.pdb -o dock.out\n\n# generate all decoys\nfor i in `seq 1 2000`; do ./decoygen lig.${i}.pdb lig.pdb dock.out $i; cat rec.pdb lig.${i}.pdb > decoy.${i}.pdb; done\n```\n\n----\n\n# Blocking target residues\n\n`block` tool (python script) is to block some residues of a receptor protein from docking.\nIf you know that some residues are not in the binding sides, please list their residue numbers and input `block` tool.\nThis program changes the name of residues to \"BLK\" and prints the new pdb on the screen.\n\n```sh\n./block [pdbfile] [chain] [target residue list]\n# ex)\n# ./block 1gcq_r.pdb B 182-186,189,195-198,204 > blocked.pdb\n```\n\nTarget residues list is separated by commas and no spaces.\nYou can also use `-` (hyphen): \"182-186\" means blocking residues of 182, 183, ..., 186.\nBlocked residues are substituted for 'BLK'.\nUpdated PDB coordinates are written to \"standard output\". MEGADOCK can only block receptor residues.\n\n----\n\n# Protein-Protein interaction prediction\n\nYou can calculates the evaluated value of Protein-Protein Interaction scores (PPI score) by using `ppiscore` command which is written in perl script.\n\n## Command Example\n\n```sh\n# 1. Docking calculation using MEGADOCK with `-t=3` option\nmegadock -R rec.pdb -L lig.pdb -o dock.out -t 3 -N 10800\n\n# -t: the number of predictions per each rotation\n# -N: the number of output predictions\n\n\n# 2. Output PPI score\n./ppiscore dock.out 10800\n```\n\n### Note\n\n`ppiscore` is compatible with re-ranking tools to get better docking candidates (e.g. [ZRANK1](http://zdock.umassmed.edu/software/)) and those tools can be used for the output files of docking calculation using megadock.\nIf you want to use such reranking tools, please refer to [our website documentation](http://www.bi.cs.titech.ac.jp/megadock/ppi.html).\n\nFor more details about `ppiscore`, please check [our webpage documentation](http://www.bi.cs.titech.ac.jp/megadock/ppi.html) or following references.\n\n----\n\n\n## References\n\n- Masahito Ohue, Takehiro Shimoda, Shuji Suzuki, Yuri Matsuzaki, Takashi Ishida, Yutaka Akiyama.    687	import hashlib, json, pathlib, urllib.request, time
   688	import pandas as pd
   689	manifest=json.loads(pathlib.Path('baseline-published/intake.json').read_text())
   690	root=pathlib.Path('data/2024-02'); root.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
   691	for item in manifest['data']['required_inputs']:
   692	    dst=root/item['name']; dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
   693	    expected=item['recorded_sha256']
   694	    def valid():
   695	        return dst.is_file() and hashlib.sha256(dst.read_bytes()).hexdigest()==expected
   696	    if not valid():
   697	        for attempt in range(3):
   698	            try:
   699	                tmp=dst.with_suffix(dst.suffix+'.download')
   700	                with urllib.request.urlopen(item['url'],timeout=120) as src, tmp.open('wb') as out:
   701	                    while chunk:=src.read(1024*1024): out.write(chunk)
   702	                if hashlib.sha256(tmp.read_bytes()).hexdigest()!=expected:
   703	                    raise RuntimeError('SHA256 mismatch: '+item['name'])
   704	                tmp.replace(dst); break
   705	            except Exception:
   706	                if attempt==2: raise
   707	                time.sleep(2)
   708	    if not valid(): raise RuntimeError('Invalid download: '+str(dst))
   709	index=pd.read_parquet(root/'index.parquet')
   710	cases=manifest['data']['cases']; selected=index[index.id.isin([c['system_id'] for c in cases])]
   711	if len(selected)!=4: raise RuntimeError('Missing or duplicate selected index rows')
   712	selected.to_parquet(pathlib.Path('data/custom_index.parquet'),index=False)
   713	prepared={}
   714	for case in cases:
   715	    row=selected.loc[selected.id==case['system_id']].iloc[0]
   716	    for role,chain in [('receptor','R'),('ligand','L')]:
   717	        src=case['apo_'+role+'_source']
   718	        if row['apo_'+chain+'_pdb']!=pathlib.Path(src).name:
   719	            raise RuntimeError('Canonical apo identity differs from intake')
   720	        dest=pathlib.Path('data')/case['prepared_record'][role]
   721	        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
   722	        # Preserve every atom/residue and coordinate. Change chain field only.
   723	        lines=[]
   724	        for line in (root/src).read_text().splitlines(keepends=True):
   725	            if line.startswith(('ATOM  ','HETATM','ANISOU','TER   ')):
   726	                line=line[:21]+chain+line[22:]
   727	            lines.append(line)
   728	        dest.write_text(''.join(lines))
   729	        prepared[str(dest)]=hashlib.sha256(dest.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
   730	        # Short aliases keep published decoygen's filename buffers within bounds.
   731	        short=pathlib.Path('data/inputs')/(case['system_id'][:4]+'_'+chain+'.pdb')
   732	        short.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
   733	        short.write_bytes(dest.read_bytes())
   734	pathlib.Path('data/prepared_sha256.json').write_text(json.dumps(prepared,indent=2)+'\n')

- **Complete tree result** contains calibration array and retained cards/records sufficient to inspect required field. On complete result, absent required card, phase or rule resolves corresponding statement false. Genuine technical failure or missing retained evidence resolves null; explain exact missing evidence next step. Never resolve unknown scientific output as false by assumption.

These lines are batched in order into boxrun commands below 32,768 characters. Every batch begins with `set -e` and `mkdir -p harness out`, runs as operation `upload` under the setup budget, and has its own receipt. A batch that fails (nonzero exit, failed fetch, missing receipt, or a timeout after its identical retry) ends the upload: later batches are not sent and the harness script does not run, and the step fails as a failed upload does today (`infra`, or `timeout` on a timeout).
